response_text: First, the user must create a pointer to the data they wish to pass to the thread and supply this pointer as an argument when calling osCreateThread or osCreateThreadWithDeadline. The OS stores this pointer in the thread control block (TCB) and uses it when initializing the thread’s stack. Specifically, the OS arranges the initial stack frame such that the value pointed to by the user is placed at the offset corresponding to register R0 in the context-switch frame. This ensures that when the thread begins execution, R0 is preloaded with the argument. This mechanism works because the ARM architecture requires that the first argument to a function must be passed in R0.\n
